title: A proximal gradient algorithm for composite log-concave sampling
abstract: arXiv:2605.12461v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We propose an algorithm to sample from composite log-concave distributions over $\mathbb{R}^d$, i.e., densities of the form $\pi\propto e^{-f-g}$, assuming access to gradient evaluations of $\alpha_f$-convex $f$ and a restricted Gaussian oracle (RGO) for $\alpha_g$-convex $g$, where $\alpha_g \ge 0$. The latter requirement means that we can easily sample from the density $\text{RGO}_{g,h,y}(x) \propto \exp(-g(x) -\frac{1}{2h}||y-x||^2)$, which is the sampling analogue of the proximal operator for $g$. If $f + g$ is $\alpha$-convex and $f$ is $\beta$-smooth, our sampler achieves $\varepsilon$ error in total variation distance using $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\kappa \sqrt d \log^4(1/\varepsilon))$ oracle calls where $\kappa := 1 \vee \beta/\alpha$, with $0\le \alpha_g \le \beta$ and $\alpha := \alpha_f + \alpha_g > 0$, which matches prior state-of-the-art results for the case $g=0$. translated_title: 一种用于复合对数凹采样的近端梯度算法
translated_abstract: 我们提出了一种从 $\mathbb{R}^d$ 上的复合对数凹分布中进行采样的算法，即形如 $\pi\propto e^{-f-g}$ 的密度，假设我们能够获得 $\alpha_f$-凸函数 $f$ 的梯度评估，以及 $\alpha_g$-凸函数 $g$（其中 $\alpha_g \ge 0$）的受限高斯预言机（RGO）。后一要求意味着我们可以容易地从密度 $\text{RGO}_{g,h,y}(x) \propto \exp(-g(x) -\frac{1}{2h}||y-x||^2)$ 中采样，这相当于 $g$ 的近端算子在采样上的类比。如果 $f + g$ 是 $\alpha$-凸的且 $f$ 是 $\beta$-光滑的，我们的采样器在总变差距离下达到 $\varepsilon$ 误差，所需的预言机调用次数为 $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\kappa \sqrt d \log^4(1/\varepsilon))$，其中 $\kappa := 1 \vee \beta/\alpha$，$0\le \alpha_g \le \beta$ 且 $\alpha := \alpha_f + \alpha_g > 0$，这与之前 $g=0$ 情形下最先进的结果相匹配。我们进一步将结果扩展到以下情形：(1) ...（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出了一种针对复合对数凹分布的近端梯度采样算法，通过结合 $f$ 的梯度评估与 $g$ 的受限高斯预言机，在 $f+g$ 为 $\alpha$-凸且 $f$ 为 $\beta$-光滑的条件下，以 $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\kappa \sqrt d \log^4(1/\varepsilon))$ 次预言机调用实现总变差距离下 $\varepsilon$ 精度的采样，匹配了 $g=0$ 情形下的最优结果。
en_tdlr: We propose a proximal gradient algorithm for sampling from composite log-concave distributions, which combines gradient evaluations of $f$ with a restricted Gaussian oracle for $g$, achieving $\varepsilon$ error in total variation distance within $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\kappa \sqrt d \log^4(1/\varepsilon))$ oracle calls, matching state-of-the-art results for the $g=0$ case.
